scenes.narration: Stress itself is not harmful. Your body was built for it. The damage comes from stress that never ends.
A short burst of pressure sharpens focus, boosts reaction time, and clears fog. That response saved lives for a hundred thousand years.
Chronic stress keeps the same chemistry switched on, so recovery never happens. Cortisol stays high while the system waits for a resolution that never arrives.
The deciding factor is control. Stress with an endpoint is manageable. Stress with no visible end is what breaks people.
You cannot always remove the pressure, but you can rebuild the ending. Small completed loops tell the brain the threat is over.
Finish something small today. Not because it matters, but because your nervous system needs to see a finish line.
